discovery: the repository is a git worktree whose shared exclude blocks the paper directory, so paper files are tracked only when staged explicitly. Under that rule 911 paper files are tracked but zero files under the upstream archive directory are, which means every recorded archive path is absent from a clean checkout.
resolution: upstream archives are treated as external re-fetchable artifacts rather than committed bytes, and every reference must carry a fetch url and a recorded digest; the quoted evidence itself is committed as extracted text

spot_verification.method: three archives and one PDF were re-fetched from the recorded url and compared with the recorded digest

gate: the validator walks the parsed structure of each receipt and requires that the same record carrying an absent archive path also carries a fetch url and a sixty-four character digest
honest_limit: a re-fetch depends on the upstream service continuing to serve that exact version; the digest proves identity when it succeeds and cannot substitute for the bytes if the service stops

gate_defect_found_and_fixed.issue: the first version of this gate scanned a character window around the reference, so a record could satisfy it by borrowing a neighbouring record url and digest
gate_defect_found_and_fixed.detected_by: a failing-first test that removed the url and digest from one record and did not fire
gate_defect_found_and_fixed.remedy: the check now walks the parsed JSON structure per record, and the same test then fired
